findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Widen the RC-safety note edit beyond its first sentence: reword 'a hypothetical v1.0.0rc1 tag', 'No rc-form tag may be pushed', and 'detect rc in the tag' in terms of dispatching with an rc `version` input / `inputs.version`, and update Scope to match.
evidence: Plan: 'The stale RC-safety note ... is corrected to say the release is dispatch-only ... its prerelease-guard constraint is unchanged.'
Plan Scope: 'docs/releasing.md — the "Tag signing" section and the first sentence of the RC-safety note.'

docs/releasing.md:582-585: 'So a hypothetical **`v1.0.0rc1`** tag would be marked *Latest* **and** published to the MCP registry ... **No rc-form tag may be pushed** unless `release.yml` first gains a prerelease guard: detect `rc` in the tag'
release.yml:4: 'Pushed tags cannot start a release.'; release.yml:12: 'The `v*` tag and GitHub Release record successful publication and do not trigger it.'
findings.finding: The plan assumes only the first sentence of the RC-safety note is stale and says the rest of the constraint is 'unchanged'. Reading the note shows that is wrong: the following sentences also assume a pushed `v*` tag starts the release ('a hypothetical **`v1.0.0rc1`** tag would be marked *Latest* **and** published', '**No rc-form tag may be pushed** unless…', 'detect `rc` in the tag'). With a dispatch-only workflow, a pushed tag starts nothing. The real risk is dispatching with `version: 1.0.0rc1`. The guard would have to check `inputs.version`, because the tag is only created after publish.
findings.location: Approach (RC-safety note correction) / Scope: 'the first sentence of the RC-safety note' — docs/releasing.md:580-586
scenarios: A maintainer follows the corrected first sentence, then reads 'No rc-form tag may be pushed', and thinks not pushing an rc tag is enough. They dispatch with version 1.0.0rc1, and the release is published to PyPI and the MCP registry and marked Latest.
Someone adds the prerelease guard to match 'detect rc in the tag' and puts it in github_release. That job runs after publish and the MCP job, so the guard has no effect.
findings.suggested_fix: In docs/releasing.md:580-586, replace the tag-push framing with dispatch framing. For example: 'a dispatch with `version: 1.0.0rc1` would be published, marked *Latest*, and sent to the MCP registry. **Do not dispatch an rc-form version** unless `release.yml` first gains a prerelease guard: detect `rc` in `inputs.version` (in `authorize`) → pass `--prerelease` (not `--latest`) and skip the MCP-registry job.' Change the Scope line to 'the RC-safety note' (the whole note, not just its first sentence).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reword the whole RC-safety note to refer to the dispatch version input (e.g. 'no rc-form version may be dispatched'; 'detect rc in inputs.version'), not tag pushes, so the note is consistent with the dispatch-only trigger.

docs/releasing.md:584-585: 'No rc-form tag may be pushed unless release.yml first gains a prerelease guard: detect `rc` in the tag'
release.yml:18-24: on: is only workflow_dispatch with a version input; release.yml:323 passes --latest unconditionally
scripts/release_guards.py: no 'rc' handling (search returned no matches)
findings.finding: The plan corrects only the first sentence of the RC-safety note ('fires on all v* tags') and calls the rest unchanged. But the remaining text also assumes tag pushes trigger releases: 'a hypothetical v1.0.0rc1 tag would be marked Latest', 'No rc-form tag may be pushed', and 'detect rc in the tag'. Under a dispatch-only trigger, pushing an rc tag is harmless. The real hazard is dispatching with version input 1.0.0rc1, because --latest is passed unconditionally and the MCP job still runs. scripts/release_guards.py has no rc check. The partial edit leaves the note internally inconsistent and pointing at the wrong action.
findings.location: Approach (RC-safety note sentence); Scope 'first sentence of the RC-safety note'; docs/releasing.md:580-586
scenarios: A maintainer reads the corrected note, sees 'no rc-form tag may be pushed', dispatches version 1.0.0rc1, and the release is marked Latest and published to the MCP registry.
findings.suggested_fix: Change Scope to 'the RC-safety note' (not just its first sentence), and reword it as: 'release.yml is dispatch-only, passes --latest unconditionally to gh release create, and runs the MCP-registry publish job. So dispatching a hypothetical version 1.0.0rc1 would mark v1.0.0rc1 Latest and publish it to the MCP registry. No rc-form version may be dispatched unless release.yml first gains a prerelease guard: detect rc in inputs.version, pass --prerelease (not --latest), and skip the MCP-registry job.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Write the doc's tag-type claim as conditional ('when no vX.Y.Z tag exists, gh release create makes a lightweight tag at the authorized run SHA; do not pre-push release tags') or add a guard that fails if the tag already exists, so the doc can't be wrong when a tag was pre-pushed.
evidence: release.yml:319-324: if release exists -> edit/upload; else gh release create "$TAG" --target "$SHA" ...
release.yml:306: 'the workflow needs no pre-pushed tag' (no guard rejects one)
Plan test asserts only 'gh release create' and 'no git tag -a'
findings.finding: The new doc text would say release tags are lightweight tags created by gh release create at the released SHA, as an unconditional rule. The workflow only guarantees this when no vX.Y.Z tag exists yet. If a tag was pushed by hand before dispatch (possibly annotated, possibly at another commit), gh release view finds no release and gh release create reuses the existing tag instead of creating one at --target $SHA. The planned test (gh release create present, no 'git tag -a') cannot detect this.
findings.location: Approach ('release tags are lightweight tags created by gh release create at the released SHA'); Testing test_docs_tag_type_matches_workflow
scenarios: A maintainer pushes an annotated v0.17.0 tag before dispatching. The release gets attached to that annotated tag, which contradicts the new doc text.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the positive assertion to the Tag section's text (heading to next heading) and anchor it on a rebar-specific phrase, e.g. 'release tags are **lightweight**' together with `gh release create`.
evidence: Approach: "The section's own peer baseline says ruff/uv/httpx use lightweight tags."
Testing: "docs/releasing.md describes release tags as lightweight" with no anchor or section scoping stated.
findings.finding: The positive assertion that docs/releasing.md "describes release tags as lightweight" is open to a substring false-positive. The same section's peer baseline already says ruff/uv/httpx use lightweight tags, so a whole-file check for 'lightweight' passes against the current, wrong doc. The RED failure would then rest solely on the negative phrase check.
scenarios: The rewrite reverts or omits the rebar-specific lightweight statement, but the test still passes because the peer-baseline sentence contains 'lightweight'.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract the section body between the '### Tag' heading and the next heading of equal or higher level. Assert it contains a fixed rebar-specific sentence fragment such as "release tags are **lightweight** tags created by `gh release create`".

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the github_release job assertion also forbid `git/tags` API calls and `git tag -a`/`-s`, and require `gh release create "$TAG" --target "$SHA"`.
evidence: Approach: "Producing an annotated tag would add a separate git-objects API call"
Approach: "release tags are **lightweight** tags created by `gh release create` at the released SHA"
findings.finding: The workflow-side check (`gh release create` present, no `git tag -a`) is narrow. It does not detect an annotated tag created through the git-objects API, which is the very alternative the Approach names. It also does not pin `--target "$SHA"`, which the rewritten doc will claim ('at the released SHA').
scenarios: A future change adds `gh api repos/.../git/tags` to create an annotated tag object, and the test stays green while the doc becomes wrong again.
findings.suggested_fix: In the job's concatenated `run` text: assert `re.search(r'gh release create "\$TAG" --target "\$SHA"', run)`. Assert `not re.search(r'git tag -[as]\b|git/tags', run)`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the test also fail if the github_release job creates a tag object some other way, e.g. a `git/tags` API call or `git tag` with `-a`/`-s`/`-m`.
evidence: "release.yml's `github_release` job creates the tag with `gh release create` and no `git tag -a`"
"Producing an annotated tag would add a separate git-objects API call (or a checkout with push credentials)"
findings.finding: The test's workflow half only checks that `gh release create` is present and `git tag -a` is absent. The plan itself names the realistic way to get an annotated tag: 'a separate git-objects API call'. Adding such a call (e.g. `gh api .../git/tags`) would make the doc false again and the test would still pass. So the test does not faithfully prove the 'doc and workflow agree on tag type' goal.
scenarios: A future change adds `gh api repos/.../git/tags` in github_release to create an annotated tag object; the doc still says lightweight, and the test stays green.
findings.suggested_fix: In the github_release job's run steps, assert that none of these appear: `git tag -a`, `git tag -s`, `git tag -m`, `git/tags`, `git push` with a tag ref.
